packageRules.description: Pin every image by digest. A tag says which version; only a digest says which bits, so a rebuilt base image carrying a patched library is otherwise indistinguishable from no change at all. It also makes a moved tag a pull failure rather than a silent substitution.

Zero-manual-work policy: every workload tracks the latest published version, majors included. The e2e smoke suite is the safety net — a break becomes a new test, never a pinned-back version. Renovate opens and auto-merges the bump once CI is green.

A workload's image reference is written ONCE, in workloads/<name>/<stage>.image. Grouping by dependency keeps a bump to the same image across a stage file and its README example in one branch. Nothing derived is touched: catalog.json is a build artifact, gitignored, regenerated wherever it is needed.
Placeholder images in illustrative code (ghcr.io/example/*, ghcr.io/acme/*) carry no real tags — never look them up.
tik and the kurly library ship calendar-versioned tags (YYYY.M.D), which the default docker versioning cannot order.

customManagers.description: Every workload's default image. The PRIMARY image of each stage lives in its own dedicated file (workloads/<name>/<stage>.image), and any secondary image (a sidecar's, a README deploy example's) in that workload's own .libsonnet or README. catalog.json carries the same reference under each stage's `runs.image`, but it is DERIVED and no longer committed — so nothing here matches it, and a bump touches only the files a person wrote. The placeholder registries are disabled in packageRules above.

Operator-backed workloads (mysql/mongodb/opensearch/cassandra clusters) pin a VERSION the operator maps to a container image, not a full image ref. Track each through a `// renovate: datasource=... depName=... versioning=...` hint above its `<name>Version='X'` line in the workload's own .libsonnet — a per-workload file, so these bumps never collide either.

The nginx image the examples and docs render with, so the illustrative manifests never pin a stale tag. Placeholder images (ghcr.io/acme/*, ghcr.io/example/*) carry no real tags and are deliberately not matched.
Alpine.js, fetched by gen-docs-data at docs-build time from the pinned version so the assembler page always ships the tracked release.
Operator versions the e2e scenarios install, pinned in hack/smoke/*.sh via a `# renovate:` comment above a `<TOOL>_VERSION="..."` line.
